procedural_history.impugned_order: Order dated 14.12.2021 in CRMM No.40058/2021 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant filed CRMM No. 40058/2021 in the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh, seeking recall as a witness in the trial before the Trial Court for further examination. The High Court rejected this prayer.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed the High Court's order to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the orders of the Courts below, and allowed the appellant's application under Section 311, CrPC for recall to be further examined as a witness. The Trial Court was directed to fix a date for the examination within six weeks, and the trial was to be concluded within nine months from the date of receipt of the Supreme Court's judgment.

directions: The application of the appellant under Section 311, CrPC for his recall to be further examined as a witness stands allowed.
The same be done on a date to be ﬁ xed by the Trial Court, within six weeks from today.
The trial will be brought to conclusion within 9 months from the date of receipt of this judgment.

issue.issue_text: Whether the courts below were justified in rejecting the application of the appellant under Section 311, CrPC for his recall as a witness in the trial for further examination.

facts: The appellant filed an application under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) to be recalled as a witness for further examination in his trial.
The appellant sought to introduce new facts related to a 'similarity of data' that became relevant only after a CFSL (Central Forensic Science Laboratory) expert had been examined.
The Trial Court and the High Court both rejected this application.
law: Section 311, CrPC grants a court discretionary power to summon, examine, or recall any witness at any stage of a trial if it is essential for a just decision.
This power is intended to enable the court to find the truth, clarify ambiguities, and ensure justice is done for all parties.
The power must be exercised judiciously, with caution, and for strong and valid reasons, not as a matter of course or to fill gaps in evidence.
The court must balance the need for the evidence against potential prejudice to the other party, uncalled-for hardship to witnesses, and trial delays.
application: The Supreme Court found that the appellant's request to be recalled was justified under the specific facts of the case.

It reasoned that the appellant had no opportunity to present the relevant facts about the 'similarity of data' during his initial deposition because the issue only arose after the CFSL expert was examined later in the trial.
The Court determined that allowing the recall would not prejudice the respondents, as they would have a full opportunity to cross-examine the appellant on the new evidence.
To address concerns about potential delays, the Court directed the trial to be concluded within a fixed timeframe.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the lower courts were not justified in rejecting the appellant's application. It set aside their orders and allowed the application for the appellant to be recalled as a witness for further examination, finding it essential for the just decision of the case.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the courts below were justified in rejecting the application of the appellant under Section 311, CrPC for his recall as a witness in the trial for further examination.
appellant_arguments: The lower courts erred in calculating the delay from the date of the initial complaint, whereas it should have been considered from the date the cause of action for the recall application arose (20.08.2021), with the application being filed shortly after on 25.08.2021.
respondent_arguments: The appellant is engaging in dilatory tactics.
The appellant should not be allowed to fill the lacunae (gaps) in their previous testimony at this stage of the trial.

cases.case_name: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Shiv Kumar Yadav
cases.principle: The discretionary power under Section 311 CrPC, while vast, must be invoked only for the ends of justice, exercised judicially with stated reasons, and not arbitrarily or capriciously.

cases.case_name: Vijay Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.principle: Section 311 CrPC consists of two parts: the first is a discretionary power for the court to summon, examine, or recall a witness, and the second is a mandatory obligation to do so if the evidence is essential for a just decision of the case.

cases.case_name: Zahira Habibullah Sheikh (5) v. State of Gujarat
cases.principle: The object of Section 311 CrPC is to prevent a failure of justice due to mistakes by either party in presenting evidence. The key factor is whether the evidence is essential for a just decision, and the court's wide power must be exercised judiciously.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The discretionary power under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which allows a court to summon or recall a witness at any stage of an inquiry or trial, must be exercised judicially and not arbitrarily. The determinative factor for invoking this power is whether the evidence is essential for a just decision of the case, with the objective of preventing a failure of justice. This power is not a matter of course and requires the court to balance the bona fide need for the evidence against potential hardship to witnesses and delays in the trial.
obiter: The power under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not limited to benefiting only the accused; it can be exercised even if the evidence supports the prosecution's case.
A party may be permitted to recall a witness to correct a bona fide error, provided the plea is made in good faith.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Supreme Court found that allowing the appellant to be recalled for re-examination would not prejudice the respondents, as they would be afforded ample opportunity to cross-examine the appellant. The court addressed the respondents' apprehension regarding potential delays by issuing a specific direction for the trial to be concluded within a fixed timeframe.
legal_tests_applied: The determinative factor for invoking Section 311, CrPC is whether the evidence is essential to the just decision of the case.
The discretionary power under Section 311 can be invoked only for the ends of justice and to prevent a failure of justice.
The power to recall a witness must be exercised judiciously, for strong and valid reasons, and with caution and circumspection, not as a matter of course.
A plea for recall must be bona fide and balanced against other considerations, including uncalled for hardship to witnesses and uncalled for delay in the trial.
policy_considerations: The object underlying Section 311 of the Code is that there may not be failure of justice on account of a mistake of either party in bringing valuable evidence on record or leaving ambiguity in the statements of witnesses.
In order to enable the court to find out the truth and render a just decision, the salutary provisions of Section 311 are enacted.
The object of the provision as a whole is to do justice not only from the point of view of the accused and the prosecution but also from the point of view of an orderly society.
A party is even permitted to correct its bona fide error and may be entitled to a further opportunity to advance justice.
